title: budgetary-scenario-catalyst-and-quant-guides
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds a scenario-driven cost tuning CLI and non-breaking defaults for quant profiles; no migration required.
description:
Motivation: teams frequently ask for a guided way to translate high-level cost objectives (budget per 1M tokens, latency SLOs, and quality thresholds) into safe batching, cache and quantization defaults. This PR introduces a small opinionated toolchain (CLI + server-side recommendations) called the Budgetary Scenario Catalyst that produces tenant-scoped suggestion bundles and human-readable guidance.

Scope: - Add a CLI subcommand 'redwood cost-catalyst generate' that accepts simple scenario inputs (budget, percentile latency, loss tolerance) and emits a candidate defaults bundle. - Implement an internal ranking function that trades off unit-economics (tokens/$), tail latency estimates, and a conservative quality penalty derived from prior evals. - Provide a set of vetted non-breaking quantization guidance profiles (qp-conservative, qp-balanced) and batch/cache safe defaults that can be surfaced in Console and used by Dedicated/Private agents. - Wire minimal telemetry events to track adoption and simulation outcomes.

What changed (high level): - CLI: pkg/cli/cost_catalyst.go, cmd/redwood/cost_catalyst/*. - Core: inference/econ/catalyst/recommender.go (ranking and safety filters). - Defaults: config/quant_profiles/*.yaml (two new profiles) and defaults/batching_safe_defaults.yaml. - Docs: docs/ops/cost-catalyst.md with usage examples and decision guidance. - Tests: integration tests that run a lightweight cost-sim over representative trace samples.

Checklist: [x] design doc referenced (Linear ENG-3421) [x] unit tests for ranking function [x] integration smoke test with simulated traces [x] docs + CLI help [x] telemetry events gated behind feature flag

Testing and rollout: Local smoke runs included in CI use a synthetic trace (tests/fixtures/trace-small.json) and assert that the suggested bundle does not reduce estimated quality below the supplied tolerance. We will roll out behind a feature flag for hosted first, enable read-only suggestions in Console, and only recommend auto-apply for Dedicated customers after a 2-week pilot. The suggestions are non-destructive by default and marked as 'proposed' in the UI.

Backward compatibility and safety: The quant profiles are additive and will not be automatically applied. The recommender uses conservative clamping rules: it will only suggest changes to batch/caching/quant that are compatible with the pinned model family and the customer's latency SLO. There are explicit opt-outs for tenants that disable automated recommendations.

Related work: draws from earlier econ heuristics (ENG-1810) and the tenant warmstart proposals; integrates with Console telemetry (PM-907).
